The Alans who stayed in the North Caucasus after the Huns broke Alan power on the steppe in the 370s. The map shows them in 400, in the plains and foothills north of the mountains.

The Alans were Iranian-speaking horse nomads, a branch of the Sarmatians. When the Huns came, some Alans joined them, others fled west and crossed into Gaul and Spain with the Vandals, and others pulled back into the Caucasus foothills. These last settled, farmed and controlled routes over the mountain passes.

In time they formed the kingdom of Alania, which grew strong around the 10th century as an ally of Byzantium. Its rulers took up Orthodox Christianity, and it dealt with the Khazars and Georgia. The Mongols destroyed Alania in 1238 and 1239, and survivors withdrew into the high valleys. Their descendants are the Ossetians, whose language is still Iranian.
